blockers: legal: UK data residency contract addendum
notes:
Background: spun out of a UK legal data provider; building an enterprise search product for law firms and in-house legal teams. Current corpus ~120M documents (contracts, filings, briefs); forecast growth to ~450M within 12 months. Primary requirement: strict UK residency for a portion of PII/contract data, EU residency for other clients.

Client quotes / chat snippets:
- CTO: "We cannot send UK client contracts outside of the UK — legal teams will not sign otherwise."
- Head of Search: "Need sub-200ms P95 for autocomplete + first-pass results in London, rerank can be async but end-to-end must feel instant."

What they want from Redwood:
- Low-latency regional search deployment in eu-west-2 (London) with fast failover to eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 for EU clients.
- Hybrid architecture: VPC-hosted private control plane for residency-sensitive tenants + dedicated GPU pools for rerank models.
- Recommendations on quantization and batching to hit cost target (goal <= $0.003 per query average across hybrid workload).
- Observability: per-route cost & latency, token-level breakdowns, audit logs for compliance reviews.

Tone of communication: pragmatic, engineering-first. Short, technical follow-ups work better than exec decks.

Sales tacticals: pricing sensitivity — prefer committed reserved capacity for steady indexing jobs, burstable for peak legal review windows. Want a staged commercial approach: POC (3 months) -> pilot (6 tenants) -> enterprise roll (all tenants).
timeline: 2025-12-01: Deep-dive with engs - discussed approximate index size and rerank strategy

requirements_summary: Workload: high-scale embeddings + reranking for legal search. Index scale: currently 120M docs, expected 300-500M. Latency targets: P50 < 50ms for vector lookup, P95 < 200ms for combined first-pass + rerank in London. Throughput: steady 200 qps with spikes to 2k qps during review windows. Cost sensitivity: target <= $0.003/query blended. Model prefs: open-weight reranker (distil-bert -> 1.5B class path) for accuracy; first-pass ANN on quantized embeddings. Routing/fallback: primary London (eu-west-2) with automatic failover to Ireland; must support per-tenant residency pinning. Security: SSO (SAML), KMS-managed keys, audit logs, contract-level data residency clauses.
